case.pattern_description: Coordinated multi-card exploitation where a specific Samsung SM-G935F device (D004630) operating behind an anonymous proxy executes unauthorized online purchases across dozens of unrelated card accounts. The device presents as new to each account and evades automated scoring thresholds by generating low model risk scores. This matches the exact modus operandi established in prior confirmed fraud cases CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3463379 scored 0.004 on the second-generation fraud model, with an expected historical fraud rate of 0.006, and legacy risk score of 0.27.

Transaction 3463379 was conducted using device D004630 ('SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080'), which was new to the card account and routed through an anonymous proxy.

Device D004630 belongs to fraud ring 36700632 and has been observed across 52 cards all time; within the 30-day window around the alert, it was used on 16 distinct cards (including C01996-K2, C08168-K1, and C10326-K1), appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy on every single card.

Device D004630 is directly implicated in four confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035), where cardholders disputed unauthorized online charges originating from this specific Samsung profile behind an anonymous proxy.
Card C09975-K1 has a baseline history of 14 prior transactions that were all online purchases under product category C, consistent with the channel and product of transaction 3463379.
The transaction amount of $48.92 was an isolated charge during the 14-day window and did not exhibit card-testing micro-authorizations or high-velocity bursts.

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Transaction 3463379 ($48.92) on card C09975-K1 was flagged due to device D004630 belonging to fraud ring 36700632. Device D004630 was new to the cardholder account, operated behind an anonymous proxy, and appeared across 16 distinct card accounts within the active 30-day window. In addition, the device is directly linked to four prior confirmed-fraud cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035). While automated model scores were low and the transaction matched the holder's baseline online category, the decisive cross-card nexus confirms coordinated undocumented abuse. The case has been escalated to an analyst, a regulatory report filed, and 15 connected cards placed on monitoring.

sar.narrative: This suspicious activity report relates to suspected coordinated card-not-present fraud conducted against card account C09975-K1, associated with customer identifier C09975. On November 16, 2016, at approximately 20:50:00 UTC, an unauthorized online transaction of $48.92 was executed on card C09975-K1 for product category C. The transaction was conducted remotely through an online channel using mobile device D004630, identified as a Samsung SM-G935F running Android 7.0 and Chrome 62.0. Device D004630 was newly registered to account C09975-K1 and utilized an anonymous internet protocol proxy service to conceal the actor's true geographic location. Internal knowledge graph analysis identified device D004630 as part of fraud ring 36700632, linked to at least 52 payment cards historically. Within a 30-day period surrounding this alert, the identical device was introduced as a new device behind an anonymous proxy across 16 distinct card accounts, including cards C01996-K2, C08168-K1, and C10326-K1. Furthermore, device D004630 has been directly linked to four prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035), in which victims disputed unauthorized online charges originating from this specific device profile. The total exposure specifically identified on card C09975-K1 is $48.92, representing part of an ongoing multi-card compromise scheme. Financial institution staff have opened an investigation, placed 15 connected card accounts under enhanced monitoring, and escalated the matter for continued analysis and mitigation.

stop_reason: The investigation concluded under policy section 6 because decisive cross-card links and direct ties to confirmed fraud cases established coordinated ring activity, meaning further automated steps would not alter the decision to escalate and file a report.
